forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: Drought moderately damages planted seedlings. Drought threatens planted seedlings at establishment: a review attributes increasing mortality of recently outplanted seedlings in dry regions to hotter and/or drier conditions intensifying planting stress, and reports high rates of seedling mortality on restoration sites in western North America [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_1, ev_establishment_survival_gross26_3]; novel levels of drought alone are attributed with causing complete restoration failure even when outplantings are used [ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_2]. In New Zealand, a community planting of native pioneer trees into former dairy pasture lost part of its young cohort to drought: survival after the 2008 drought within the 2007 planting averaged 78% across all species [ev_climate_shock_laughlin18_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: In Australia a dry spell at planting did not significantly affect sapling survival at four months, a mild event in the authors' own description [ev_drought_hazard_preece23_1]. The rest of the evidence is second-hand statements from high-income or unspecified settings, the complete-failure claim comes from a perspective piece not specific to forests, and the only survival figure is the New Zealand planting, a single site that does not separate drought deaths from other causes [ev_climate_shock_laughlin18_1]. The Spanish dryland project whose mortality tracked a drought index has moved to the plantation family's drought row.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: The compiler for dune stabilisation and afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan judges it to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1529_2012_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating, not a measurement of storm damage to plantings, from a desert dune setting in an upper-middle-income country outside the low-income target [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1529_2012_local_rainstorm]. The Uganda tree-planting rating sits in the plantation family's row. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: A review of reforestation in tropical developing countries, citing an earlier study second-hand, lists uncontrolled fires, together with uncontrolled grazing, weed competition and cutting for fuel, fodder, poles and lumber, among the main causes of reforestation failure [ev_fire_hazard_le12_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: one second-hand narrative statement that does not separate fire from the non-climatic causes and does not quantify the damage [ev_fire_hazard_le12_1]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: In Australia, flooding rains that followed Cyclone Yasi flooded newly planted plots and drowned most saplings, and a perspective on restoration notes that a record drought followed by a year of heavy rain and flooding can cause high seedling mortality [ev_flood_hazard_preece23_1, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_3].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The compiler for floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan rates the technology as coping well with river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1509_2011_general_river_flood], so flood-adapted species and sites change the picture. The literature units are narrative from high-income or unspecified settings and the perspective piece is not specific to forests.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: Outplanted seedlings on open restoration sites are exposed to air at seedling height 10 °C hotter than at 2 m, with soil or litter surfaces up to 30 °C hotter, which causes heat stress, and even minutes of extreme heat can cause seedling mortality in many species [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_2, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The evidence is review-level and from western North America or unspecified settings, with the perspective piece not specific to forests; the microclimate effect arises after the overstorey is removed by harvest or fire.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for community protection of micro-basins through reforestation in Honduras judges it to cope well with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_750_2016_landslide].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measurement of landslide damage to planted stands [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_750_2016_landslide]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: In Brazilian restinga, total mortality of planted seedlings over four years did not differ significantly between seasonally flooded depressions and dry sandbanks [ev_establishment_survival_loureiro21_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: This is a single site study in a sandy coastal plain, and both habitats had substantial mortality, so the null finding concerns the added effect of seasonal flooding only.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: In Brazilian restinga, strong and constant wind causes branches to break and other damage to seedlings, directly affecting height growth [ev_climate_shock_loureiro21_1]. The Cabo Verde compiler judges afforestation as not coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1523_2011_local_windstorm].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: Compilers for dune afforestation in Turkmenistan and reforestation in Honduras judge coping with windstorms or cyclones as good or moderate [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1529_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_750_2016_extratropical_cyclone, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_750_2016_tropical_storm]. The Brazilian statement cites earlier work and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements. The Spanish tree-shelter losses, the Vietnam smallholder-plantation typhoon evidence and the Uganda rating have moved to the plantation family's wind row.

forest_restoration__active_planting__bio.mechanism: Both directions are reported. On the gain side, planted stands create habitat and attract seed dispersers: beneath framework-species plantings in northern Thailand thirty-six tree seedling species recruited naturally, 25 of them animal-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1], and the WOCAT compiler for dune afforestation in Turkmenistan rates habitat diversity as raised, noting that the vegetation on the barkhan sands now provides habitat for 25-27 species of plants and animals [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity]. On the loss side, a pantropical review warns that where forests can regenerate naturally or with some assistance, tree planting can reduce biodiversity conservation benefits if the species or management chosen do not provide suitable habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__bio.conditionality: What separates the gain side from the loss side is what the land would do without planting. The cautions apply where forests can regenerate naturally and where the species or management chosen do not provide suitable habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1]; the gains are on bare dunes and degraded tropical land with no unplanted control [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity]. The actionable reading is a siting and design choice: planting looks favourable where nothing would regenerate otherwise, and risky where natural regeneration is possible unless the species and management provide habitat. Both sides remain thin. The loss side is a single review warning, not a measured comparison; the gain side is a compiler rating and a case study without a control. Plantation comparisons sit in the plantation family's biodiversity row, which is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up.

forest_restoration__active_planting__car.mechanism: Planting native trees on former pasture in Brazil's Atlantic Forest built up carbon storage in biomass and litter of 21.85, 25.78 and 38.29 Mg/ha in successively older plantings, against 138.94 Mg/ha in mature forest [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3]. The Honduras compiler notes that the change in agrarian land use into forests reduces carbon and greenhouse gas emissions [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_750_2016_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases], and a review of nature-based solutions states that afforestation increases topsoil carbon in carbon-poor soils [ev_soil_organic_carbon_seddon21_5].
forest_restoration__active_planting__car.conditionality: The young Brazilian plantings held only 15.7 to 27.6% of reference-forest biomass [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_4]; that comparison with mature forest is held out of the class as a reference shortfall, but it shows how far young plantings remain from the baseline they restore toward. The same review marks where planting reverses the sign: the soil disturbance associated with afforestation causes significant losses in carbon-rich soils, especially of the deep soil carbon that takes many decades to accumulate [ev_soil_organic_carbon_seddon21_5], and afforestation on peaty soils can lead to losses of soil carbon that outweigh that sequestered as the trees grow [ev_carbon_sequestration_seddon21_7]. These are review sentences carrying cited findings rather than new measurements. Apart from the Brazilian stock measurements the evidence is a compiler rating, and soil organic carbon enters this row as a component proxy. Site choice is the lever: avoid peaty and carbon-rich soils.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cat.mechanism: Reviews of reforestation and afforestation find water yield falling. A UNESCO review of moist tropical forest hydrology reads catchment studies, including work in sub-humid Fiji and South Africa, as showing a decline in water yield after forestation of degraded grass- or cropland with pines or eucalypts, caused by higher evaporative loss from tall vegetation in rainy spells and higher transpiration in dry periods [ev_water_yield_bruij90_3]. An FAO synthesis states that the effects of reforestation or afforestation on water yields are usually the reverse of those for forest removal, and that low flows are usually diminished as well, especially where fast-growing, heavy water-using species are employed [ev_water_yield_ham08_5, ev_water_yield_ham08_6]; planting forests on open land where the water table is close to the surface will lower groundwater levels [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_2]. A global review warns that large-scale afforestation in water-limited environments will inevitably exacerbate water scarcity [ev_water_yield_zhang17_7]. The gain side is modelling: under full reforestation potential, water yield increased in 7 of 15 Asia-Pacific regions, significantly in four, by 11.4%, 16.9%, 17.6% and 84.9% [ev_water_regulation_teo22_1, ev_water_regulation_teo22_2, ev_water_regulation_teo22_3, ev_water_regulation_teo22_4], and spruce reforestation of a Heihe River headwater was predicted to increase annual runoff by 8.6% [ev_water_yield_zhang17_6].
forest_restoration__active_planting__cat.conditionality: What separates the sides is method and species. The losses are review statements about reforestation and afforestation in general and about planting with pines, eucalypts or other fast-growing, heavy water-using species [ev_water_yield_bruij90_3, ev_water_yield_ham08_6]; the gains are model projections for large regional reforestation scenarios rather than project-scale planting, and the same model shows nonsignificant declines in other regions where heightened evapotranspiration outstrips increases in precipitation [ev_water_regulation_teo22_5]. The lowered water table under new forest is also described as improving drainage, so on waterlogged land it is not purely a loss [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_2]. The pine and eucalypt decline is the review's reading of other studies, and its source table is not readable, so it gives a direction without a size [ev_water_yield_bruij90_3]. Measured paired-catchment losses after afforestation, and the review report that China's Grain-for-Green programme reduced water supply, sit in the plantation family row, which is parked out of the roll-up; check that row before assuming that restoration planting avoids them. This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.mechanism: Tree planting and soil preparation are cited at US$1,400 to 34,000/ha across restoration initiatives [ev_project_cost_crouzeilles17_1]. In Brazil, direct seeding and seedling planting cost approximately ten times more (about US$2000/ha) than less intensive approaches, mostly due to the higher input costs [ev_project_cost_branc19_1]. A World Bank irrigation and watershed project in Madagascar estimated US$1,500 per hectare for reforested area [ev_project_cost_exact14_1]. Other reported establishment costs run from restoring rain forest corridors in Madagascar to native-species reforestation in Chile and Colombia, reforestation in Costa Rica, eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil, and WOCAT afforestation sheets in Honduras, at US$5,402.39/ha, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, at US$6,078.79/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_4, ev_project_cost_wri17_8, ev_project_cost_wri17_9, ev_project_cost_wri17_10, ev_project_cost_wri17_7, ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_establishment].
forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.conditionality: The cost class rests on the entries in the low- and lower-middle-income band: the Honduras sheet, the Madagascar corridor figure and the Madagascar project estimate; the Brazilian survey figure is upper-middle income and stays out of that range [ev_project_cost_branc19_1]. The Madagascar project figure is a planning estimate used in a carbon-accounting tool's worked example, not a measured cost [ev_project_cost_exact14_1]. Most figures carry no stated price year, the Brazil table entry mixes eucalyptus with native species, WOCAT costs are compiler-entered and converted from local currency, and the cited range spans restoration initiatives rather than a single project.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.mechanism: The abatement cost of plantation reforestation combines implementation cost, the opportunity cost of land and carbon accumulated, net of revenue from selling harvested wood products, giving a modelled median of US$23.00 per tCO2 [ev_project_cost_busch24_4].
forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.conditionality: This is a single modelled estimate with a wide interdecile range, from US$-14.80 (plantations profitable without carbon payments) to US$724 per tCO2, so the figure is a screening value rather than a project budget, and it depends on wood-product revenue that a restoration (non-harvest) planting would not earn.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.mechanism: In a mulching experiment in tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, polyethylene mulch cut the cost of each established plant, including nursery costs, from 18.00 USD on bare soil to 2.45 USD, because 92 of 180 plants established against 10 of 180 without mulch [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. The saving comes from survival: the mulch costs money, but far more plants establish, so the cost per surviving plant falls.
forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.conditionality: Organic mulches lowered cost per established plant much less, to 12.50 USD with alfalfa straw and 13.33 USD with leaf litter [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. This row rests on one experiment at one tropical dry forest site, with costs in USD and no wider cost comparison, so the figures indicate the direction of the saving rather than a transferable value.

forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.mechanism: The only unit is a regional model of large-scale reforestation in water-insecure parts of the Asia-Pacific, in which extremely dry months became less likely in 9 of 15 regions [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: one modelled source at landscape scale, and most regional changes in the source's table were not significant and one basin moved in the adverse direction [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1]. It says nothing about plot-scale planting or measured drought impacts on rural livelihoods. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.mechanism: In a regional land-climate model, reforestation reduced the probability of extremely dry months in 9 of 15 Asia-Pacific regions, especially where it also increased total annual precipitation [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single modelling study of reforestation at landscape scale, not observed project outcomes, and most regional changes were not significant [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1]. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__fir.mechanism: The Uganda tree-planting compiler rates fire risk as unchanged, commenting that dense forest brings fire risk that is common in the neighbouring Kiruhura district but not yet a problem in Rubagano [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_fire_risk].
forest_restoration__active_planting__fir.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating, and its comment implies fire risk may rise as planted canopy closes rather than fall. No measured evidence on planting and fire is in the pool.

forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.mechanism: Planted forest lowers flood peaks moderately in this evidence, and mainly locally. Catchment models in Slovakia and Luxembourg show reforestation and afforestation lowering flood peaks: in Slovakia a reforestation scenario cut a simulated peak from 84.8 to 74.9 m3/s and, for a 50% increase of forest, reduced peaks by about 24% on average, more for short storms than long ones, and an earlier scenario converting all arable land in a basin to forest cut peak flow by 42.3% [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. A UNESCO review of moist tropical forest hydrology states that the beneficial effects of reforesting, terracing and contouring degraded lands on stormflow and peakflow are evident at small-basin scale [ev_flood_hazard_bruij90_6]. An FAO synthesis expects flash flooding to be reduced locally for frequent short, low-intensity storm events where soils are deep [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_7], and a global review states that afforestation in energy-limited environments will help to reduce flood risks [ev_flood_hazard_zhang17_1]. A systematic review of forest cover and catchment flooding finds that afforestation yields gradual reductions in peak flow, shaped by forest maturity and spatial distribution, with peak flow in small catchments falling by up to 14% and only minor differences in mean reductions across event intensities up to the 1% AEP event [ev_flood_hazard_herath25_2, ev_flood_hazard_herath25_4, ev_flood_hazard_herath25_5].
forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.conditionality: What separates the benefit from the nulls is scale and storm size. The same FAO synthesis finds no evidence that reforesting watersheds reduces or prevents floods except at the very local scale of a few hundred hectares [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_5, ev_flood_hazard_ham08_6]; a Himalayan analysis concludes that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on local flooding, and certainly not on the Ganges and Brahmaputra mainstreams [ev_flood_hazard_ives87_1]; and a conference overview from the same lead author warns that reforestation in the mountains conceived as a palliative for the problems of the plains is likely to reap only disappointment [ev_flood_hazard_ivesmt87_1]. These are review and position statements rather than measurements. The UNESCO review's statement bundles reforesting with terracing and contouring, is limited to small basins, and gives no size because its supporting table cannot be read [ev_flood_hazard_bruij90_6]. Much of the benefit weight comes from high-income temperate catchment models at landscape scale, so transfer to low-income settings is weak, and the modelled benefit becomes less as rain continues [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3]. The largest figure is a secondary citation with no basin named [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. The flood-cover review stresses that these afforestation reductions are smaller than the rises in peak flow that follow deforestation, rests on limited small-catchment data, and pools other studies' modelled scenarios from mostly temperate catchments; its 1% AEP reading is the only one at an extreme event, and it is modelled [ev_flood_hazard_herath25_2, ev_flood_hazard_herath25_4, ev_flood_hazard_herath25_5]. No unit from a low-income setting measures flows or flood damage after planting. For farmers the effect is off-site, arriving downstream of the planted land.

forest_restoration__active_planting__foo.mechanism: The only unit is the compiler for afforestation in Cabo Verde, who rates food self-sufficiency as unchanged, noting that afforestation reduces the options of land use [ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency].
forest_restoration__active_planting__foo.conditionality: No class can be stated: the row holds a single compiler rating and nothing that measures hunger, food consumption or food self-sufficiency after planting [ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. The rating flags a real trade-off, since planted land can be taken out of food production, but it is not a finding of no effect. A second independent source, or a measured food-security outcome for households near afforested land, is needed.

forest_restoration__active_planting__hea.mechanism: In China, afforestation of former grassland and cropland lowered average daily land surface temperature by 0.5 and 0.4 degrees C compared with adjacent unplanted land, because some of the daytime cooling is offset by nighttime warming [ev_microclimate_buffering_peng14_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__hea.conditionality: This is a single study, and it splits by rainfall: in areas with 400 to 600 mm of rain a year, nighttime warming almost cancels the daytime cooling from afforesting grassland [ev_microclimate_buffering_peng14_2], so planting in dry areas may bring little or no cooling. The comparison is between planted forest and nearby grassland or cropland at one point in time, not before and after planting. It measures annual land surface temperature, not heat stress on crops, livestock or people, and the strength is not stated.

forest_restoration__active_planting__pro.mechanism: The compiler for dune afforestation in Turkmenistan rates fodder production as strongly increased, because the planted sand fixing species are also used as forage [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_fodder_production].
forest_restoration__active_planting__pro.conditionality: No class can be stated: the row holds a single compiler rating, not a measured yield, and fodder is only a component of the production gap; no unit reports crop yields under active planting [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_fodder_production]. A second independent source, or a measured crop or livestock output near planted land, is needed.

forest_restoration__active_planting__rec.mechanism: Recurrent costs are the annual maintenance of planted stands: compiler-entered maintenance for community microbasin reforestation in Honduras and for karst afforestation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and a table entry of US$775/ha per year for eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wri17_11].
forest_restoration__active_planting__rec.conditionality: WOCAT figures are converted from local-currency entries by compilers and the Brazil table states no price year; only the Honduras sheet falls in the low and lower-middle income band, so the recurrent-cost picture for poorer contexts rests on a single sheet.

forest_restoration__active_planting__rur.mechanism: Planting programmes can raise rural incomes through subsidies, off-farm work and returns on restoration designs, but the evidence gives only the direction and a slight effect. China's Sloping Land Conversion afforestation programme increased off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_iufro20_9], and the programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__rur.conditionality: Livelihood losses are documented and are the measured harm on this row: reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection on the land to be reforested without viable alternatives [ev_household_income_le12_1]. The gains come from upper-middle-income China and Brazil, so they transfer to poorer settings only by analogy; the Amazon returns are modelled for agroforestry restoration designs, and the Chinese ratio counts socioeconomic outcomes only and is cited in a systematic review [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1, ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]. Every unit reaches poverty through income or return proxies, and none quantifies the size of the effect on households. Food-security ratings sit on the food-insecurity row, and plantation results are on the plantation family's poverty row.

forest_restoration__active_planting__soi.mechanism: Planted cover reduces runoff and soil loss on the restored slope and catchment, so the benefit reaches farmers off-site, through less sediment and runoff arriving downslope and downstream rather than on the plot itself. In Pakistan a watershed restoration of tree planting, control of grazing and erosion control structures reduced storm runoff and sediment yields by 55 and 78% [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_1, ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1], and Chir pine planting with elimination of grazing at Balakot reduced surface runoff by 57% and sediment production by 69% against adjacent grazed areas with natural vegetation [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2]. A review of Chinese vegetation restoration finds it could reduce soil erosion by at least 80% once vegetation cover exceeds 60% [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1]. A Slovak catchment model shows reforestation decreasing surface runoff [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1], and in Ethiopia tree planting on degraded catchments reduced annual runoff depth from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. A UNESCO review of moist tropical forest hydrology states that tree planting, like soil conservation measures, may well reduce the sediment from surface erosion and shallow land slips entering the drainage system [ev_sediment_retention_bruij90_13].
forest_restoration__active_planting__soi.conditionality: The Pakistan results are bundles - planting with grazing control and, in the watershed study, check dams and spillways - so the reduction cannot be credited to planting alone [ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1, ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2].
