None of the three ratings states a mechanism.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The sources give nothing that separates the two sides: no site, soil or design detail is attached to any rating. One visible difference is that the Tunisian technology includes planting acacia, whereas both Ethiopian ratings, one on each side, are for closure alone [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage]. All three are practitioner ratings with no measured drainage, so this row records a disagreement among compilers rather than a tested effect.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: The compiler for an Ethiopian area closure rates wind velocity as strongly reduced as vegetation recovers on the closed land [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1414_2011_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating of everyday wind speed; it says nothing about cyclone or storm damage to people or to the regenerating stand.

forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.mechanism: On a Mediterranean dryland reforestation project in Spain, the drought index correlated strongly with the course of plantation mortality (r = −0.72); about one quarter of the plantation was dead by the first year and more than half in the second, and the trend worsened in an exceptional, severe drought [ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_1, ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_2]. In a plantation trial on pasture in Tabasco, Mexico, a drought soon after planting came on top of other stresses, and bare-root Cordia dodecandra survival fell to 33% and 22% in the two planting methods [ev_establishment_survival_keyes97_2].
forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.conditionality: The evidence comes from just two studies, one in a high-income dryland, and the strength is not quantified. The Mexican authors put the losses mainly down to the seedlings being transplanted twice and moved a long way from the nursery, with the drought added on top, so drought alone did not cause them [ev_establishment_survival_keyes97_2]. The authors add that an extreme drought can reveal, several years later, the impact of inappropriate technical measures that would otherwise remain concealed, so the losses mix drought with planting technique [ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_3]. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda judges it to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1577_2013_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating, not a measurement of storm damage to plantings [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1577_2013_local_rainstorm]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.mechanism: Wind damages planted stands once storms pass a threshold, and the damage grows quickly above it. A review of wind damage to planted and managed forests suggests damage starts when canopy-top hourly wind speeds exceed approximately 8.5 m s−1 and gusts outside the forest exceed 25–30 m s−1, with damage increasing almost exponentially as gust speed rises [ev_climate_shock_gardiner21_1]. The same review finds that in the same storm a taller, more mature stand is generally more likely to fail than a shorter younger one [ev_climate_shock_gardiner21_2], that new gaps or edges from thinning, harvesting, clear-cutting upwind stands or roads leave the remaining trees particularly vulnerable [ev_climate_shock_gardiner21_3], and that the effects last for years through further wind or insect damage to weakened trees or reduced growth [ev_climate_shock_gardiner21_4]. In central Vietnam typhoon damage is a continuing concern for smallholder plantations and leads planters to favour short rotations [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1]; on a Spanish dryland reforestation project, windstorms blew away tree shelters [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1]; and in the south-eastern United States, Hurricane Michael (October 2018) caused over $2 billion in losses to the timber industry in Florida, Alabama, and Georgia [ev_climate_shock_wiener20_1].
forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.conditionality: The class is slight because the field evidence describes manageable losses: the Vietnam evaluation adds that typhoon risk has so far not discouraged smallholders from planting, the Spanish losses were partly put down to poor tethering, and the Uganda afforestation compiler judges the technology to cope well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1, ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1577_2013_local_windstorm]. The hurricane figure is a loss total for commercial timber in a high-income country, cited second-hand in a survey paper, with no per-hectare figure, so it shows the direction of the threat but not its size for a project [ev_climate_shock_wiener20_1]. The review's thresholds come from planted and managed forests mostly in high-income countries and cite other studies; it notes that no definitive global values can be given because site and forest conditions differ [ev_climate_shock_gardiner21_1]. Management changes the risk: rotation length, thinning and where edges are created all matter [ev_climate_shock_gardiner21_2, ev_climate_shock_gardiner21_3]. Read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline. Tree species matters too: a survey paper notes that longleaf pine stands withstand hurricanes better than loblolly or slash pine, though those reach maturity faster [ev_climate_shock_wiener20_2]; this is cited second-hand from a rich country.

forest_restoration__plantation__biodiver.mechanism: The findings that set the rating point toward a small biodiversity loss, but none states how large it is. A review of nature-based solutions states that if non-native tree plantations replace intact native ecosystems such as ancient grasslands, peatlands or woodlands, the outcomes for biodiversity will be poor [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_1]. On the Orissa coast of India, extensive Casuarina plantations established as a storm protection measure caused destruction to olive ridley sea turtle nesting beaches [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badola05_12]. A review of coastal tree belts reports, partly from earlier work, that in India sand dunes have been flattened to make way for Casuarina plantations, destroying sea turtle nesting habitat, that Casuarina roots can prevent turtles from nesting above the high tide line, and that Casuarina is known to harm tropical birds and invade mangroves [ev_biodiversity_outcome_feagin10_2]. A review of coastal tree belts in Vietnam argues that plantings of non-native species may damage native ecosystems, noting, second-hand, that Casuarina tends to invade mangrove forests in low-salinity settings [ev_biodiversity_outcome_veettil21_2]. The nature-based solutions review also reports research in north-west India showing that although afforestation activities can lead to an aggregate increase in forest cover, in most cases they result in loss of diversity and promote monocultures [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_4]. Against this, the review allows a gain in a narrower case: establishing plantations of non-native trees in a highly degraded landscape might benefit biodiversity locally if the trees enable native vegetation to regenerate, or regionally if plantations take pressure off native biodiverse forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_2]. An INRAE expert synthesis's own small meta-analysis of species richness in plantations against natural regeneration of the stand after regeneration cutting finds no clear difference: -0.24, a very imprecise estimate from a very small number of cases, with an interval that spans zero [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1]. Cited Canadian studies compared plantations with forest left to regrow after clear-cutting: spruce plantations had less rich and less diverse moss communities [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_5], while hybrid larch plantations had significantly richer plant communities and hybrid poplar plantations showed no clear difference [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_4].
forest_restoration__plantation__biodiver.conditionality: The loss is stated without a size: the loss-side units are review statements and a cited case, none of which measures the decline against the land a plantation replaced, so the row reports a direction only. What separates loss from gain is what the plantation replaces: intact native ecosystems, a nesting beach or a diverse cover replaced by monocultures on the loss side [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_badola05_12, ev_biodiversity_outcome_feagin10_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_4], a highly degraded landscape where the trees help native vegetation return on the gain side [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_2]. Both coastal reviews are second-hand for most of their harm statements, and the Vietnam review hedges its warning as something that may happen [ev_biodiversity_outcome_feagin10_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_veettil21_2]. The pooled comparison against regeneration is not significant [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1], and the Canadian results differ by tree species and by group of plants, and are second-hand [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_4, ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_5]. Three further units point toward loss but are held out of the class because they compare plantations with reference native forest rather than with the starting point of a project: a global meta-analysis found tree plantations supported on average 29.3% lower species-specific abundance than reference native forests (95% interval 22.0 to 35.9%) [ev_biodiversity_outcome_hua22_1], INRAE states that plantations generally lead to decreases in biodiversity, or at least to changes in composition at the expense of native species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6], and it cites a 40% loss of local species richness in forest plantations relative to uncut control forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2]. These describe a shortfall from a natural baseline, not a restoration effect. The INRAE evidence is temperate and boreal, and only the Indian cases come from the low- and lower-middle-income target. The plantation family is kept out of the forest-restoration roll-up, because plantation monocultures may not count as a nature-based solution, and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__carbon_s.mechanism: Plantations moderately increase carbon storage. Planted forests and woodlots accumulate carbon quickly in their early decades: compiled measurements give planted-forest removal rates of 4.5 to 40.7 t CO2 per hectare per year in the first 20 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_1], and IPCC default tables give above-ground growth of tropical plantations from about 5 to 20 tonnes of dry matter per hectare per year depending on zone and continent [ev_carbon_sequestration_ipcc19_8, ev_carbon_sequestration_ipcc19_7]. Soil organic carbon rose by 26% on average under afforested former cropland in a global review [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_1]; the same review found soil carbon up approximately 12% under eucalyptus and pine and more than 25% under other broadleaf trees [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_11, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_12], and the Uzbekistan compiler reports surface biomass growth of 20 t per hectare per year [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1533_2011_biomass_above_ground_C].
forest_restoration__plantation__carbon_s.conditionality: The class is held at moderate because few of the units that agree on direction state a size. The IPCC values are compiled defaults carried forward from earlier guidance, in dry matter rather than carbon, and the Uzbekistan figure is a compiler's statement. The soil gain is not universal: afforestation in the boreal zone caused an average soil-carbon loss of about 1.5% [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4], soil carbon did not change on low-clay soils [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_7], plantation density made no measurable difference [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_10], and other conifers had little effect on soil carbon (2%) [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_13]. A global meta-analysis found plantations held 32.8% less above-ground biomass than reference native forests (95% interval 16.5 to 45.9%) [ev_carbon_sequestration_hua22_1]; that is a comparison with natural forest, not with the land a plantation replaced, so it is held out of the class, but it shows plantations store less than the forest they might stand in for. The plantation family is kept out of the forest-restoration roll-up. A Mexican planting trial that reports high seedling survival (95% to 100%) is counted here, but it measures survival, not carbon [ev_establishment_survival_keyes97_1].

forest_restoration__plantation__catchmen.mechanism: Plantations strongly cut the water leaving a catchment. Afforesting grasslands and shrublands reduced annual runoff on average by 44% and 31%, with proportionally larger reductions for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]; on former grassland, eucalypts cut runoff by 75% and pines by 40% [ev_water_yield_farley05_5, ev_water_yield_farley05_6]. In Fiji, planting Caribbean pine in dry-zone grasslands resulted in dry-season streamflow reductions of 65 percent [ev_water_yield_ham08_7], and in South Africa, where nearly all plantations are on previously native grasslands, water reductions are in some cases felt as soon as two years after planting [ev_water_yield_ham08_10]. A review reports that China's Grain-for-Green programme used mainly fast-growing non-native species that have reduced water supply [ev_water_yield_seddon21_10], and that single-aged, low diversity, intensively managed plantations may reduce water availability in arid regions [ev_water_yield_seddon21_9]. A national model for New Zealand finds new radiata pine forests on pasture and tussock reduce water yield by between 30% and 50%, through increased interception of rainfall and evaporation by the canopy [ev_water_yield_dymond12_2].
forest_restoration__plantation__catchmen.conditionality: These are afforestation and plantation-forestry results, mostly from paired catchments where grassland was replaced by fast-growing exotic stands; the authors suggest the effects will be more severe in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_4], and in South Africa the largest decreases come early and then diminish [ev_water_yield_ham08_10]. The New Zealand figure is modelled [ev_water_yield_dymond12_2], and the Grain-for-Green result is a review sentence carrying cited findings. Two units compare plantations with natural forest rather than with the land planted, so they are held out of the class as reference shortfalls: native-species plantations aged 25 to 45 years produce dry-season streamflow deficits exceeding 50% relative to old-growth forest [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_3], and a global meta-analysis found 13.4% lower water yield in tree plantations than in reference native forests (95% interval 4.1 to 21.9%) [ev_water_yield_hua22_1]. The plantation family is kept out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.mechanism: In a plantation trial on pasture in La Chontalpa, Tabasco, Mexico, semi-mechanised planting cost US$178/ha against US$217/ha by hand [ev_project_cost_keyes97_1, ev_project_cost_keyes97_2], and a nearby Cedrela odorata plantation was reported to cost US$236.3/ha to establish [ev_project_cost_keyes97_3]; plantation establishment in the Masoala corridors of Madagascar is listed at 279 dollars per hectare [ev_project_cost_wri17_3]; and modelled implementation cost for plantations across low- and middle-income countries has a median of US$3,729/ha, inclusive of replanting after harvest cycles, against US$140/ha for natural regeneration [ev_project_cost_busch24_2].
forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.conditionality: The cost class is set by the Madagascar entry, the only one in the low-income band; the Mexican and modelled figures sit outside it. The Cedrela figure is cited second-hand from a thesis [ev_project_cost_keyes97_3]. The trial figures from Mexico are historical field costs for establishment and first-year maintenance that exclude donated seedlings, and the modelled median counts replanting over harvest cycles, with an interdecile range of US$1,530–11,675/ha [ev_project_cost_busch24_2]. These are production-plantation costs, not the cost of restoration toward a natural baseline. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.mechanism: Modelled across areas feasible for plantation in low- and middle-income countries, the abatement cost of climate mitigation through plantation, accounting for revenue from the sale of harvested wood products, has a median of US$23.00 per tCO2, with an interdecile range of US$−14.80 to 724 [ev_project_cost_busch24_4].
forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a cost class: one modelled source, and the figure nets out wood-product revenue, which is why its range reaches below zero [ev_project_cost_busch24_4]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__fire__al.mechanism: There is not enough evidence to say whether plantations raise or lower fire risk. A review of nature-based solutions warns that planting trees on fire-adapted savannah and dryland grassland risks much greater carbon losses in intensely hot plantation fires, whereas those grasslands recover readily from their usual cooler fires, and that planting can also raise the risk of fire on peatland in temperate regions [ev_fire_hazard_seddon21_8]. The practitioner for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates fire risk as unchanged so far, but notes that dense forest brings a fire risk that is common in a neighbouring district [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_fire_risk].
forest_restoration__plantation__fire__al.conditionality: The warning comes from a review sentence that reports other studies rather than measuring fire, and it concerns planting that replaces fire-adapted open land or peat [ev_fire_hazard_seddon21_8]. The Uganda entry is a practitioner rating of no change, with a warning, not a measurement [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_fire_risk]. Neither gives a size. A measured fire record from planted stands, or a second independent source, is needed before a rating can be given. Read this row as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward natural forest.

forest_restoration__plantation__flood__a.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates downstream flooding as reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__plantation__flood__a.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, a judgement rather than a measured flood record [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__flood_ha.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates downstream flooding as reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__plantation__flood_ha.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measured flood record [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__rural_po.mechanism: Timber and protective plantations moderately raise household income in this evidence. In Vietnam a World Bank evaluation found the economic rate of return for smallholder plantations was 13.2% at completion, against 17.0% expected at appraisal [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1], and the financial gains for participating smallholders were substantial, mainly because low-interest loans from the project reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_household_income_ieg18_1]. In Costa Rica, payments for environmental services on reforested land made up 18.66% of participants' income during the contract [ev_household_income_padilla17_1], other Latin American studies cited there found payments reach around 10% of family income [ev_household_income_padilla17_2], and participants' perceived economic benefit scored 63.9% of the maximum, mainly from covering planting and upkeep costs, family employment and secure land title [ev_household_income_padilla17_3]. A global cost analysis finds plantations would be profitable even without carbon payments across 28.3% of the area where they are feasible [ev_economic_return_busch24_1]. In Andhra Pradesh, India, a review reports, from the project's own material, returns from Casuarina coastal plantations of Rs. 25,000/ha (USD 600/ha) after 4 years, shared half with the community and half reinvested in more planting, plus access to fuelwood and small timber [ev_household_income_feagin10_3].
forest_restoration__plantation__rural_po.conditionality: No source measures a change in poverty itself: the evidence is rates of return, profitability and income shares. The Vietnamese gains depended on subsidised loans [ev_household_income_ieg18_1], the Costa Rican income comes from the payments rather than the timber, and the 63.9% figure is a perception score [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3]. The global profitability figure is a model and says nothing about who benefits [ev_economic_return_busch24_1]. The Indian figure is second-hand from the project's own reporting, and the review notes that cutting trees for fuelwood works against the plantations' protective purpose [ev_household_income_feagin10_3]. Only the Indian case is from a lower-middle-income country; Costa Rica and Vietnam are upper-middle-income.

forest_restoration__plantation__soil_ero.mechanism: The plantation evidence points both ways, so no direction is stated. Under good tree cover erosion falls: in eucalyptus afforestation in Calabria, Italy, sediment concentrations were substantially greater on a plot with little or no tree cover, confirming the importance of the forest canopy in reducing erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1]. In New Zealand, converting pasture to production forest cuts landslide erosion: in the Waipaoa catchment, calculated landsliding for 1990 and 1995 conditions suggests reforestation over that period produced a 10% decrease in sediment from landslides, equivalent to a 2% decrease in suspended load, and a scenario reforesting the 66 km2 of pasture in the most susceptible areas would cut landslide sediment inputs by 20% [ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_1, ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_4]; a national model finds new radiata pine forests, once mature, generally reduce mass-movement erosion by an order of magnitude [ev_erosion_hazard_dymond12_1]. Erosion can also worsen under plantations: particularly serious erosion problems arise in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3], and an FAO synthesis names dense, planted monocultures with little or no understorey and ground cover as experiencing increased surface erosion rates [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_4].
forest_restoration__plantation__soil_ero.conditionality: What separates the sides is the erosion process and the ground layer under the trees. The gains are on mass movement and on erosion where canopy and cover are good: mature stands reinforce slopes against landslides, and sediment falls under good tree cover [ev_erosion_hazard_dymond12_1, ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_1, ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1]. The losses are surface erosion where understorey, vegetation and litter are absent, cleared or collected [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3, ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_4]. The actionable reading is a management condition, keeping understorey and litter, rather than a property of plantations as such. Both loss statements come from syntheses rather than measurements and state no comparator, and the gain side is a high-income Italian catchment study and New Zealand models: the Waipaoa calculation assumes a lower landslide frequency under forest, its targeting result is a scenario, and the national model's benefit applies once forests are mature and pauses after harvest while roots decay [ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_1, ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_4, ev_erosion_hazard_dymond12_1]. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline. A global meta-analysis found plantations gave 60.6% less erosion control than reference native forests [ev_erosion_hazard_hua22_1]; that compares plantations with natural forest, not with the land planted, so it is held out of the rating.

forest_restoration__plantation__water_qu.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates downstream siltation as decreased, the sediment pathway to water quality [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__plantation__water_qu.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single compiler rating, and siltation is only a component of water quality; no unit measures water quality directly [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_siltation]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__waterlog.mechanism: In Uzbekistan, the compiler for afforestation to rehabilitate degraded irrigated cropland rates excess-water drainage as improved at +3, through bio drainage through transpiration [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1533_2011_excess_water_drainage].
forest_restoration__plantation__waterlog.conditionality: No class can be stated: the row holds a single practitioner rating, not a measured water table, for trees planted on waterlogged irrigated cropland [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1533_2011_excess_water_drainage]. A second independent source, or a measured water-table response under plantation, is needed. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__wind_cyc.mechanism: A study of the Bhitarkanika mangroves reports, citing earlier work, that extensive Casuarina plantations established as a storm protection measure along the Orissa coast were ineffective in preventing damage, and that they caused destruction to olive ridley sea turtle nesting beaches [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_11].
forest_restoration__plantation__wind_cyc.conditionality: This row is data deficient: it rests on a single cited statement, not a measurement, so it is described here but does not set a class. It records a coastal plantation that failed as storm protection and harmed a nesting habitat; it says nothing about how much damage it failed to prevent. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__production_gap.mechanism: Where restoration narrows the production gap, it does so through cropland downstream of or next to restored land, and through fodder; on the restored land itself, soil nitrogen can fall. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than those beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2]. In Brazil the Reflorestar payments programme raised agricultural value added by 8% and the value of agricultural production by approximately 14% in the poorest quarter of municipalities [ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_3]. A preprint review, not yet peer reviewed, finds that increases in forest cover led to higher landscape-scale agricultural productivity in 95% of reported cases, with gains from 0.4% to 79.5% [ev_crop_yield_yang24_1]. WOCAT compilers give the on-farm pathways: an Ethiopian area closure raised crop production because soil depth increased and soil fertility improved, Tanzanian enclosures raised crop production through mulching materials, fodder through area enclosure and decline of forest fire, and animal production through nutritious cut and carry pastures, and in Turkmenistan the planted sand fixing species are also used as forage [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1072_2011_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1607_2014_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1607_2014_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1607_2014_animal_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_fodder_production]. On the other side, a meta-analysis found that returning cropland or bare land to forest left soil total nitrogen not significantly changed overall (3.04%), but that it decreased by 16.84% in hot regions and by 19.85% in humid regions compared with cropland, which the authors attribute to higher plant uptake of soil nitrogen [ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_4, ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_6, ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_7].
forest_restoration__production_gap.conditionality: The sub-practice rows disagree, so no direction is stated. The natural regeneration row reads a strong gain from the Tigray exclosure yields [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2], while the cross-family row is itself conflicted, with the Brazilian programme and preprint gains set against the soil nitrogen losses [ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_3, ev_crop_yield_yang24_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_6, ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_7]. What separates them is where production is measured and the climate: the gains are crop, fodder or production-value results on farmland beside or downstream of forest, while the nitrogen losses, the measured harm on this row, describe the soil of land converted from cropland to forest in hot or humid regions. The nitrogen units are part of the production picture, not a yield measurement. The Tigray advantage was concentrated in the drier year, with no statistically significant yield difference in the second production year (2024/2025), and it concerns downstream cropland compared with open grazing [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4]. The Brazilian gains apply to the poorest quarter of municipalities in an upper-middle-income state and come from a payments programme [ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_2]. The preprint's forest cover gain is not a named restoration practice [ev_crop_yield_yang24_1]. The WOCAT units are compiler ratings rather than measured yields.

forest_restoration__production_gap__inco.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings, closing degraded land to grazing and letting vegetation recover strongly lifts production on nearby farms. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures achieved notably higher crop yields than those next to open grazing areas in the 2023 season, by 188 to 222 kg/ha, and a panel estimate controlling for soil fertility, labour and fertilizer put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2]. The advantage was greater in the first, drier year [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3]. WOCAT compilers add the pathways: an Ethiopian area closure raised crop production because soil depth increased and soil fertility improved [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1072_2011_crop_production], and Tanzanian enclosures raised crop production through mulching materials, fodder through area enclosure and decline of forest fire, and animal production through nutritious cut and carry pastures [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1607_2014_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1607_2014_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1607_2014_animal_production].
forest_restoration__production_gap__inco.conditionality: The measured evidence is a single Ethiopian study, and its gain is on cropland downstream of the exclosures compared with farms beside open grazing, not production on the closed land itself. The gain depends on the year: no statistically significant yield difference was found in the second production year (2024/2025) [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4], so the strong reading rests mostly on a drought-affected season. Both yield estimates come from the same households using different methods. The Tanzanian and Ethiopian WOCAT units are compiler ratings, not measured yields, and fodder and animal production are parts of the production picture rather than crop yield.

forest_restoration__production_gap__inco.mechanism: In these upper-middle-income settings the evidence points both ways. On the gain side, farm output rose alongside restoration: under Brazil's Reflorestar payments programme, agricultural value added in the poorest-quartile municipalities rose by 8% and the value of agricultural production by approximately 14% [ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_3], and on Turkmen barkhan sands the compiler rates fodder production as strongly increased because the planted sand-fixing species are also used as forage [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_fodder_production]. On the loss side, a meta-analysis of vegetation restoration in erosion zones found that returning cropland or bare land to forest left soil total nitrogen content not significantly changed overall (3.04%), and that it decreased by 16.84% in hot regions (MAT > 15 °C) and by 19.85% in humid regions (MAP > 800 mm) compared with cropland; the authors attribute this to higher plant uptake of soil nitrogen under high temperature and rainfall [ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_4, ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_6, ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_7].
forest_restoration__production_gap__inco.conditionality: Studies disagree, and what separates them is what is measured and where. The gains are production value and forage on farmland and planted dunes [ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_3, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_fodder_production]; the losses are soil nitrogen on land converted from cropland to forest, confined to hot and humid regions, with no significant change across all sites [ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_4, ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_6, ev_soil_nitrogen_yang23_7]. The nitrogen units are a component of the production gap rather than a yield measurement, the meta-analysis does not report where its studies were, and its subgroup significance is shown only in a figure. The Brazilian result is a municipal-scale programme effect confined to the poorest-quartile municipalities and measured as production value rather than yield; it reflects a payment programme rather than a restoration practice alone, so the route from trees to farm output is not shown [ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_2]. The Turkmen unit is a practitioner rating, and its gain is forage from the planted shrubs, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_fodder_production].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: For a bundled programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries under sustainable forest management in India, the WOCAT compiler judges the works to cope well with local rainstorms and thunderstorms but only moderately with hailstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_hailstorm].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: all three ratings come from the same technology sheet, so they count as one source, and they are compiler judgements, not measurements of damage [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_hailstorm]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: The India compiler judges a village-protected programme of broadleaf plantations and assisted regeneration as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5243_2019_forest_fire].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single practitioner judgement on a bundled programme, where coping is likely to reflect active protection by villagers rather than fire tolerance of the stands; it does not show the stands are undamaged by fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5243_2019_forest_fire]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: The compiler for the Khost learning site in Afghanistan judges the technology as not coping well at all with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_7460_2024_flash_flood].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single practitioner judgement from a site that bundles several land and forest management practices, so the rating is not specific to forest protection, and it gives no description of the damage and no measurement [ev_asset_flood_wocat_7460_2024_flash_flood]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for a bundled programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries under sustainable forest management in India rates the works as coping moderately with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5243_2019_landslide].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measurement of landslide damage [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5243_2019_landslide]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__bio.mechanism: Protection and community forest management retain and expand forest habitat. GEF sustainable forest management projects show less deforestation than matched areas without projects [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], and forest cover increased by 8% under community management in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. A global analysis of community forests found environmental condition improved after community forest management in 56% of the 524 cases tracking it [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1]. WOCAT compilers rate diversity as increased under protection: in India plant species diversity rose with improved moisture availability, soil conditions and microclimate, and the area provides more water and habitat for small animals and birds [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_animal_diversity]; in Afghanistan migratory animals and birds returned due to the protection measures and the prohibition of human activities [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity]. Forest governance instruments retain forest habitat: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]. World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity under participatory forest management, and less deforestation under Bank-supported payment schemes in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1], and in Bolivia most payment-like initiatives showed marked or intermediate environmental protection effects, and the rest weak ones [ev_biodiversity_outcome_robertson05_1]. The same systematic review's pooled estimate for forest cover under protected areas, across 14 estimates, finds more forest retained than on comparable unprotected land (Hedges' g of 0.17), though with high heterogeneity (I-squared 96 percent) across the pooled studies [ev_landscape_forest_cover_malh25_2].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__bio.conditionality: Most units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction, a component proxy for biodiversity, and the Mexican figure is a before-after comparison with no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. In south-west Madagascar transfers of management to communities were found superficial and unable to stop forest clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and GEF project sites likely exposed to urban encroachment showed forest losses [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]; the GEF evidence concerns existing forest under a bundle of protection and management rather than restoration. Governance effects are uneven: in the global community-forest analysis environmental condition decreased in 32% of community-forest cases [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1]; In the same Indian Himalayan village-council (Van Panchayat) forests, crown cover of broad-leaved forest did not differ significantly from neighbouring state-managed forest, a direct boundary comparison for pine forest likewise found no significant difference, but a propensity-score-matched comparison across the whole sample found council-managed pine forest had significantly higher crown cover than matched state forest [ev_landscape_forest_cover_somanathan09_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_somanathan09_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_somanathan09_3]. This is a comparison of both management regimes for forest that already exists, not a restoration of cleared or degraded land. An evaluation of Vietnam's special-use forests found no clear-cut evidence that the project improved biodiversity, noting that its tracking tool was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. These governance units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction rather than species, the Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in a systematic review, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored. That is a biodiversity-component proxy (forest cover, not species counts) for existing protected forest rather than restoration, and the review itself notes it is less confident the pooled effect generalises across contexts given that heterogeneity [ev_landscape_forest_cover_malh25_2].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__car.mechanism: Protecting and managing forest keeps carbon stored in standing biomass and lets more build up. GEF sustainable forest management sites sequester more carbon each year than their counterfactual and avoid deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management reduced deforestation in Nepal and increased forest cover in Puebla, Mexico [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], environmental condition improved after community forest management in 56% of the 524 cases tracking it in a global analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1], and the India compiler states that carbon storage is increased by the plantation, citing an average sequestration rate of 3.5 t ha -1 yr-1 for Van Panchayat forests [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and municipal management in Bolivia by 0.80 [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; protected areas retained more forest than comparable unprotected land (Hedges' g of 0.17) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_malh25_2]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation under participatory forest management [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. A global model finds existing secondary forests kept standing could remove 20.7 MgC per hectare on average over their best 25-year window, against 18.8 for new regeneration [ev_carbon_sequestration_robinson25_2], and that 8-year-old forest in the Brazilian Amazon would remove 36% more carbon by 2030 than newly growing stands (10.5 versus 7.7 MgC per hectare) [ev_carbon_sequestration_robinson25_3]. A global model of natural climate solutions finds that avoiding the conversion of existing forest offers the second largest maximum and cost-effective mitigation potential, with relatively low uncertainty (±17%) [ev_carbon_sequestration_griscom17_10].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__car.conditionality: The class is held at moderate because the only size estimates for carbon come from models: the forest-keeping comparison is a model of above-ground carbon in existing secondary forest, not measured removals [ev_carbon_sequestration_robinson25_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_robinson25_3], the GEF carbon estimate is also derived from a model over existing forest [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1], and the global avoided-conversion pathway is a model that states its size only in a figure, adding that costs may matter less than public policy challenges where land tenure is unclear [ev_carbon_sequestration_griscom17_10]. Much of the rest is forest-cover change standing in for carbon, and the India figure is a compiler's citation of earlier work [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. Several units found no effect: community management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], and a boundary comparison of crown cover under Van Panchayats found no significant difference from neighbouring state forest [ev_landscape_forest_cover_somanathan09_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_somanathan09_2], though a matched whole-sample comparison found pine crown cover higher under council management [ev_landscape_forest_cover_somanathan09_3]. Some GEF sites showed harmful outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3], condition decreased in 32% of community-forest cases in the global analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1], the Mexican result has no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], and the protected-area pool varies widely across contexts (I-squared of 96 percent) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_malh25_2]. All of this evidence is about existing forest, not restored forest, and the Nepal, Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in systematic reviews.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cat.mechanism: Forests use more water than the land cover that replaces them, so standing forest passes less water downstream. As both natural and human-established forests use more water than most replacement land cover, even partial forest removal increases downstream water yields [ev_water_yield_ham08_1], and replacing forest cover with other land uses almost always results in increased runoff and streamflow [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_2]; a UNESCO review of moist tropical forest hydrology calls it beyond doubt that both natural and mature man-made forests use more water than most agricultural crops or grassland [ev_water_yield_bruij90_1]. A worldwide review of paired catchments found that forest cutting consistently gave more total water yield, in proportion to cutting intensity, because tall forests evaporate and transpire more; Hamilton retells it in both his earlier essay and his later FAO synthesis, so it counts once [ev_water_yield_ham87_1, ev_water_yield_ham08_4]. Reported first-year increases after forest clearance range between 110 and 825 mm, depending on local rainfall, and converting lowland rain forest to well managed grassland or annual cropping may produce permanent increases of 200 - 300 mm a year [ev_water_yield_bruij90_1, ev_water_yield_bruij90_2]. The extra flow arrives through the year: in most tropical small-basin experiments the bulk of the increase came in the dry season or baseflow [ev_water_yield_bruij90_15], the FAO synthesis puts the greatest percentage increase in the dry season, citing that review among others [ev_water_yield_ham08_2], and Hamilton's essay reports increased flows throughout the year, including the dry season [ev_water_yield_ham87_2]. Daily late-summer flows rose by up to 300% after experimental harvest, though most daily changes were 50% or less [ev_water_yield_jon12_2]. Global syntheses agree: more forest cover loss tends to increase annual runoff in both large and small watersheds [ev_water_yield_zhang17_1], an increase in forest coverage reduces the share of rainfall leaving as runoff [ev_water_yield_zhou15_1], and changes to forests in water-limited watersheds can lead to larger water-yield responses [ev_water_yield_zhou15_2]. Harvesting or removing forest also raises groundwater levels [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cat.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the protected land itself holds more, and it can coexist with the local gains recorded in the protection water stress row. Every unit compares existing forest with its harvest, clearance or loss, which is why the row sits in the protection family and not in the forest restoration roll-up; none measures the outcome of a protection or community forest management project. Two results run the other way. Where infiltration after forest removal is degraded so far that extra stormflow exceeds the baseflow gain, diminished dry-season flow is the result [ev_water_yield_bruij90_16]; the dry-season gains above come from controlled experiments where infiltration was kept, so this is the case they leave out. Very small summer events also decreased by more than 40% in the first 2 years after canopy removal in the fog-prone Fox Creek basins [ev_water_yield_jon00_1]. Nulls stay named: 12 (of 61) large and 33 (of 252) small watersheds showed no significant change in annual runoff despite forest cover loss [ev_water_yield_zhang17_4], and basins of 7 to 727 km2 on Hainan and the 14500 km2 Pasak basin in northern Thailand showed no systematic streamflow change despite extensive forest loss; the review expects detectable change mainly where forest is replaced by annual cropping rather than left to regenerate [ev_water_yield_bruij90_9]. The groundwater statement also cuts both ways: removal can move soil salts into the rooting zone [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_1].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.mechanism: Costs cover establishing community-managed forest and protection works: compiler-entered establishment costs on WOCAT sheets for an afforested community forest with plantation and fodder nursery in India and for a protected area in Afghanistan, and a WRI table entry for community management of forest resources with sustainable fuelwood production in Benin.
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.conditionality: The WOCAT figures are compiler entries, the Indian one converted from local currency and spread over mixed plantation and nursery areas, and the Benin figure comes from a project database with no price year; these packages include planting and infrastructure, so they are not the cost of protection alone.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.mechanism: Two payment schemes report low programme costs per tonne of carbon: the PAS scheme in Brazil was estimated at 0.56 USD per ton of CO2, and the Ugandan scheme cost $0.57 per ton of delayed emissions against an estimated social benefit of $1.11 per ton, roughly two times the cost [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3]. A global spatial model estimates the break-even carbon price at which carbon payments would cover the land opportunity costs of conserving most remaining mangroves, avoiding release of their stored CO2 [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_2].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.conditionality: The Brazilian figure is a total programme cost given without assessing cost-effectiveness, and the Ugandan cost-benefit ratio is a simple calculation; both come from single schemes cited in a systematic review [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3]. forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: one measured finding from one Indian state [ev_project_cost_somanathan09_1]. It compares the recurrent cost of administering existing forest under both management regimes, not the cost of restoring land, and gives no figure that transfers to another setting. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding from a restoration context.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__dro.mechanism: Forest protection and community management keep the water regulation that standing tree cover provides and give households a forest income to fall back on. An FAO synthesis states that it is well established that partial or complete removal of the tree cover accelerates water discharge, increasing the risk of drought in the dry season [ev_drought_hazard_ham08_1]. In India, a programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries is rated as strongly decreasing drought impacts because improved surface and subsurface hydrological functioning in the upper watershed increased springshed groundwater stores and enhanced stream and spring flows in the dry season [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_drought_impacts]. In Malawi, households taking part in forest co-management through village natural resource management committees had 57% higher annual forestry income after a rainfall shock than non-participants [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_4], and under shocks the per capita income gain from participation showed up among moderately poor households, at 31.4% [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_7].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__dro.conditionality: The moderate class is set by the measured Malawi survey, which brings the row down from the strong practitioner reading. The co-management benefit is confined to forest income: participation did not mitigate the effect of rainfall shocks on non-forestry income, which shocks are likely to erode by 36% among participating households too, and this no-benefit result is what discounts the class [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_5]. The per capita gain under shocks reached moderately poor households rather than the poorest, and the authors report it as shifting away from the poorest decile [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_7]. The FAO unit describes what existing forest does, framed as the cost of losing it; it enters this protection row through the existing-forest comparator and is a review-level statement with no size attached [ev_drought_hazard_ham08_1]. The Indian unit is a practitioner rating from a technology sheet that bundles planting, regeneration and protection, so the effect cannot be attributed to protection or community management alone [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_drought_impacts]. No unit covers severe or extreme drought, and the Malawi study defines its rainfall shock from rainfall records rather than an author-described drought event. forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__fir.mechanism: Protecting and managing standing forest lowers the chance that it burns. The India compiler reports that villagers protect the intervention area from anthropogenic and wild fires, so the forest rehabilitated faster and has a lower risk of burning because of greener cover and less flammable pine-needle accumulation [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_fire_risk]. A World Bank evaluation of participatory forest management projects lists reduced incidence of fires among the environmental outcomes reported where those outcomes were monitored [ev_fire_hazard_ieg13_1]. A rapid systematic review of ecosystem-based disaster-risk-reduction interventions in low- and middle-income countries pools protected-area evaluations from Brazil, Colombia and Madagascar and finds protected areas reduce forest-fire occurrence against comparable unprotected land, a pooled effect (Hedges' g) of 0.32 [ev_fire_hazard_malh25_1]. A preprint review, not yet peer reviewed, cites a study finding that converting tropical forests to agriculture increases fire risk fourfold [ev_fire_hazard_yang24_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__fir.conditionality: Most of this evidence is about keeping existing forest, not restoring it. The pooled estimate is for natural forest kept under legal protection, and a study among those it pools found the reduced fire inside the protected forest came alongside more fire in the densely populated buffer zone just outside it, a leakage effect the pooled estimate does not count [ev_fire_hazard_malh25_1]. In a multi-country study of children in rural areas, Rasolofoson et al. find that high exposure to forests causes children to have at least 25% greater dietary diversity than no exposure, an average difference of 0.4 points (95% confidence interval 0.29 to 0.51) against matched non-forest households, and raises the share of households where children ate vitamin A– or iron-rich food by at least 11 and 16 percentage points [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_1, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_2, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_3, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_4]. A global forest and food-security assessment cites Ickowitz et al. (2014), who found children's dietary diversity rising with community tree cover across 21 African countries, and Johnson et al. (2013), who found that children in Malawi communities that experienced deforestation had less diverse diets [ev_food_security_iufro15_2, ev_food_security_iufro15_1]. Naidoo et al. find that living near multiple-use protected areas with documented tourism would increase children's height-for-age growth scores by 9.8% and reduce the likelihood of stunting by 13.4% [ev_food_security_naidoo19_1]. In India the WOCAT compiler for broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries reports better village self-sufficiency from more and better fodder and more water [ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In a global satellite comparison, deforestation led to consistent warming of annual land surface temperature of 0.38 degrees C in tropical regions and 0.16 degrees C in temperate regions [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_5]. The outdoor-work finding is a model of what clearing forest costs, compared with places that kept forest [ev_heat_stress_hazard_parsons21_1]. The reviews report other studies' findings, and two of those findings come from model-based attribution rather than direct measurement [ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_4, ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_5].
