The benefit reaches farmers through the surrounding landscape, not on their own plots.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__hea.mechanism: Standing forest keeps the land surface cooler than cleared land, and protection keeps that cooling; the benefit is small and its size for heat stress is not stated. Satellite and flux tower data show tropical forest surfaces significantly cooler than nearby cleared areas, by 0.2–2.4 degrees C a year (mean 0.96) [ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_1], and temperate forest cover cools by 0.02–1.0 degrees C (mean 0.4) [ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_2]. A worldwide satellite comparison finds tropical forests 2.41 degrees C cooler than nearby open land over the day, and mid-latitude forests 0.27 degrees C cooler in the northern hemisphere and 0.97 in the southern [ev_microclimate_buffering_li15_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_li15_2]. In the tropics, places that lost forest between 2003 and 2018 saw afternoon temperatures in the hottest months rise by 1.6, 1.2 and 0.55 degrees C in the Americas, Africa and Asia, against 0.2, 0.4 and -0.01 where forest was kept [ev_microclimate_buffering_parsons21_1], and the time each day that is unsafe for heavy outdoor work rose by 0.33, 0.13 and 0.16 hours [ev_heat_stress_hazard_parsons21_1]. Deforestation led to warming of 0.38 degrees C in tropical and 0.16 in temperate regions [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_5]. In an Indonesian village survey, the most common reason villagers gave for why forests matter to health was that forests keep the environment cool [ev_microclimate_buffering_wolff18_1], and a cited Sumatran study found primary and secondary forests more than 4 degrees C cooler than nearby young oil palm plantations [ev_microclimate_buffering_wolff18_2]. Trees can keep cooling through long heatwaves thanks to deeper roots [ev_microclimate_buffering_ellison17_1], and a review reports that extremely hot days are significantly more common following deforestation [ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_3], that historical deforestation explains about a third of the increase in the intensity of the hottest days [ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_4], and that it has made hot dry summers two to four fold more frequent and intense [ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_5].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__hea.conditionality: One unit shows the opposite: boreal forests warm the surface by 0.79 degrees C over open land [ev_microclimate_buffering_li15_3], and boreal deforestation led to slight cooling of -0.04 degrees C [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_5], so the cooling holds for tropical and temperate settings, not boreal ones. In mid latitudes daytime cooling is largely offset by night warming [ev_microclimate_buffering_li15_2]. Every unit describes existing forest compared with open or cleared land; none evaluates a protection or community forestry project, and none measures restored forest. The Indonesian villager answers are perceptions, not measurements [ev_microclimate_buffering_wolff18_1], and the Sumatran figure is cited second-hand [ev_microclimate_buffering_wolff18_2]. The outdoor-work figures come from a model of what clearing forest costs, against places that kept forest [ev_heat_stress_hazard_parsons21_1]. Most of the evidence is land surface temperature, which is more sensitive than the temperature of the air at 2 m [ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_2], not heat stress on crops, livestock or people, so the strength of the effect on heat stress is not stated. The heat-extreme findings are a review reporting other studies, two of them from model-based attribution [ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_4, ev_microclimate_buffering_lawrence22_5].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__pro.mechanism: The units describe what existing forest does for nearby farming, or what is lost when it is cleared. A preprint review, not yet peer reviewed, finds that 87% of sites saw a decrease in agricultural productivity, from 2.8% to 55.1%, after forest cover loss [ev_crop_yield_yang24_2], and cites a study in which deforestation in Indonesia led to a 45% decline in local agricultural productivity [ev_agricultural_production_value_yang24_1]. It cites Brazilian Amazon studies in which forest conservation policies reduced deforestation by 45–56% and increased cattle productivity by 14–36% [ev_livestock_productivity_yang24_1], and in which a 10% rise in upstream forest cover led to a 3.2% increase in milk production through better water regulation, which improved pasture and cow health [ev_livestock_productivity_yang24_2]. Its own country-level model suggests cereal yields decline once forest loss passes about 48% [ev_crop_yield_yang24_3].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__pro.conditionality: No class is set. All five units come from one preprint and describe the value of forest already standing, or the cost of losing it, rather than what protection or community management adds; the engine treats such units as the opportunity cost of existing use, which cannot set this row. Most are other studies' findings cited second-hand, and the 48% threshold is a projection from current trends. What is missing is a measured comparison of farm production with and without a protection or community forestry project.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rec.mechanism: Recurrent costs are compiler-entered annual maintenance costs per hectare on WOCAT sheets for the community forest package in India and the protected learning site in Afghanistan [ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance]. A payment scheme in Costa Rica is estimated to spend between $255 and $382 per year per hectare of additional forest [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rec.conditionality: The two compiler entries differ widely, the Indian one is converted from local currency and spread over mixed plantation and nursery areas, and neither sheet itemises maintenance tasks [ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance]. The Costa Rican figure is payment spending per hectare of additional forest rather than a maintenance cost, from an upper-middle-income country, and is cited in a systematic review [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rur.mechanism: Protection and community forest management moderately reduce poverty through forest income and employment. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation across 18,000 community forests [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2], 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1], and community forestry in Madagascar had a small but beneficial impact on living standards [ev_household_income_iufro20_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1]; a meta-analysis of counterfactual studies finds small gains in local monetary outcomes (g = 0.028) and poverty outcomes (g = 0.117) [ev_household_income_kandel22_1, ev_rural_poverty_kandel22_1]; households in the Chitwan National Park buffer zone of Nepal have 19 percent higher per capita income [ev_household_income_kandel22_2]; and living within 10 km of protected areas with tourism lowers the likelihood of poverty by 16.1%, with poverty 8.8% lower near multiple-use protected areas [ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_1, ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_2]. Co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent and by 66% for low-income households, consumption in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. Around Malawi's forest reserves, taking part in co-management is associated with 17.48% more forestry income and 21.07% more non-forest income [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_1, ev_household_income_kimwanga26_2], 26.6% higher per capita income among the poorest households without rainfall shocks [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_6], and, after shocks, 57% higher forestry income [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_4] and a 31.4% per capita income gain for moderately poor households [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_7]; participants also owned more durable goods [ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_9, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_10, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_8, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_12, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_13]. World Bank support raised participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh poorer households compensated for lost land access gained 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. Community forestry in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member [ev_household_income_ceballos21_1], households near GEF sites in Uganda show income gains [ev_household_income_gefieo19_1], groups selling environmental services in Bolivia improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1], and non-timber income rose after benefit-sharing at Bach Ma, Vietnam [ev_household_income_ieg18_3].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rur.conditionality: The pool is divided. The global community-forest review that reports income gains in 68% of cases also records 26% with no change and 6.3% with decreases [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1]. In south-west Madagascar community management contracts were not profitable and did not raise incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; the GEF forest-management portfolio has a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 [ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, local studies found no effect of REDD+ on material well-being, and an analysis in Indonesia found potentially harmful effects [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6]; payment programmes have a small beneficial or neutral effect on poverty [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]; and Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2]. Benefits skew to the better-off: in Nepal poor and low-caste households receive much less while bearing more costs [ev_household_income_iufro20_3]; near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests forest income rose by an insignificant 2 per cent and lowest-quartile households lost 6 per cent and 10 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; at Bach Ma benefits were shared unevenly and products over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. After rainfall shocks, Malawi participants held fewer durable assets than non-participants around Mua-Livulezi, a 2.846 unit decrease, and Vwaza Marsh, a 1.677 decrease [ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_11, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_14], participation did not stop shocks eroding non-forestry income by 36% [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_5], and the study compares members with non-members at a single point in time rather than before and after. Just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their livelihood aims, and benefit-sharing around Vietnam's special-use forests, averaging US$1,053 per community, was too small to have any discernible impact [ev_household_income_ieg13_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_2]. A large household survey adds that forests are a weak safety net: only 7.8% of households turned to forests as their main response to an income shock, 10.4% to any wild resource [ev_household_income_wunder14_1]; that unit is carried but does not set the class. The protected-area studies measure what living near standing forest provides, not a restoration outcome; the Colombian benefit of $411–1,236 per hectare a year is a carbon valuation, not cash income [ev_economic_return_wri17_3]; and many figures are review citations or World Bank estimates without a comparison group.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__soi.mechanism: This row describes the soil and slope protection that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. Forest cover provides the most effective barrier to natural erosion, and loss of forest cover to other land uses always increases human-accelerated erosion unless soil conservation is carried out [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_2]; converting forest to sedentary agriculture or grazing can greatly increase both surface and mass erosion, especially with mechanical clearing [ev_erosion_hazard_ham87_10]; and in the Ethiopian highlands soil loss under forest averaged 1 tonne per hectare, the lowest of seven categories of land use [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_3]. Land managers and scientists agree that forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and to a lesser extent deep-seated movements, in upland areas [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7]; a UNESCO review of moist tropical forest hydrology attributes the fewer shallow (less than 1 m) mass movements on forested hillslopes to the slope stability a well-developed tree root network imparts [ev_erosion_hazard_bruij90_11]. Clearing removes that protection: in a US study area the number and acreage of slides increased four and one-half or more times after logging began in 1953, and the scarcity of slides on timbered slopes near logged areas strongly indicates increased susceptibility from logging [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_1, ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_2]; investigations in steep forested terrain worldwide note up to a 10-fold increase in landslide erosion roughly 3–15 yr after timber harvesting, and rates of mass erosion can rise two- to more than ten-fold 3-15 years after harvest [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4]; on sites prone to shallow landslips, root decay after cutting can raise the risk of slope instability until replacement root systems develop [ev_erosion_hazard_ham87_9]; mean suspended sediment at managed Sabah catchments was several times higher in the most affected period after logging than before it [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_3]; and in Japan most landslides happened in young forest stands, shrublands and grasslands, the preventive function of the forest increasing with its age class [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_4]. In New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment, deforestation resulted in a 25-fold increase in areal landslide frequency for a 600-mm storm and a 5-fold increase for a 260-mm storm, and on Wharekopae lands, where 35 slides would have been expected had the sampled forest been pasture during storms of 184, 187 and 195 mm, none were observed [ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_2, ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_3]. The WOCAT compiler for community forests in India rates soil loss and downstream siltation as decreased, noting that trees and other vegetation helped mitigate displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands and helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation], and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes reported by participatory forest management projects where monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__soi.conditionality: The row carries one harm finding, on how the protection works: experimental evidence cited in Hamilton's essay shows raindrop impact on bare soil under tree canopies greater than 10 m in height is greater than on bare soil in the open; what protects the soil from splash and sheet erosion is the organic matter, the surface litter and the low vegetation, not the canopy [ev_erosion_hazard_ham87_7]. Where litter or understorey is removed, tall forest does not by itself protect the soil. The same essay holds that it is not the cutting of trees as such that causes large increases in on-site erosion, but the way the products are removed [ev_erosion_hazard_ham87_8]. Root protection has a depth limit. Deep-seated slides do not seem to be influenced appreciably by the presence or absence of a well-developed root network [ev_erosion_hazard_bruij90_12], the role of forests for deep-seated landslides is considerably less, and during extreme events with copious rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]. Downstream sediment is slow to respond: for watersheds of more than 10,000 ha, off-site sediment will not be reduced for decades by maintaining forest cover, although on-site benefits may be immediate [ev_sediment_retention_ham87_11]. The Waipaoa comparisons set forest against values predicted for pasture, from a forest sample covering a small share of the land studied, and the authors find forest's protection grows with storm size, which sits against the Thailand null below [ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_2, ev_erosion_hazard_reidpage03_3]. Nulls stay named: in Thailand landslide density appeared independent of vegetation cover, the storm magnitude overwhelming the stabilising influence of root strength [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_4]; a cited study found lumbering had no part in contributing to slide occurrence and suspected forest maturity of slightly raising slide probability [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_3]; and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The logging, harvest and land-use comparisons are evidence about what existing forest does and what its loss costs, not the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme, which is why they sit in this family and not in the restoration roll-up [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_1, ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_2]. The India units are compiler ratings from a sheet that bundles several practices. Benefits fall largely off-site for farmers, as fewer slides and less sediment downslope and downstream.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.mechanism: There is not enough evidence to rate this. The practitioner for community forests in India rates downstream siltation as decreased, saying the works helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. An essay on Himalayan deforestation adds a limit: for watersheds of more than 10,000 ha, the downstream sediment benefit of keeping forest cover will not show for decades, because sediment goes into storage, while benefits on the site may be immediate [ev_sediment_retention_ham87_11].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.conditionality: The Indian entry is a practitioner rating of siltation, which is only part of water quality, from a sheet that bundles several practices, with no measured data [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. The essay is a judgement about existing forest, not a measurement [ev_sediment_retention_ham87_11]. A measured sediment or water-quality result from a protected or community-managed forest is needed before a rating can be given. Any effect is off-site for farmers, arriving downstream.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.mechanism: Practitioners in India and Afghanistan rate water quantity and availability as improved, which together give a moderate benefit: the Indian practitioner cites better soil water-holding capacity from slower runoff and improved overall water storage [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity], and the Afghan practitioner, who rates only a slight increase, cites water seeping into the ground through revegetation and improved land cover, recharging the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability]. Peak-flow evidence from harvest experiments sits in the flood rows, following the project ruling that peak-flow damping is flood mitigation, not water supply.
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.conditionality: Both ratings come from sheets that bundle several practices (broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries in India; a learning site for sustainable land and forest management in Afghanistan) with no measured flow or groundwater data, so the gain cannot be credited to protection alone, and they are practitioner ratings, not measurements. Benefits to farmers come from soil water and groundwater fed by the protected land, off-site from the farm. Whether keeping forest standing changes the water passed downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__win.mechanism: Two sources point to a strong reduction in cyclone damage, but neither measures it. A review of coastal tree belts in Vietnam, citing an earlier study, states that coastal forests are effective at reducing wind speed during low and medium cyclones [ev_windbreak_protection_veettil21_1]. In India, a WOCAT compiler for a programme of plantations, assisted regeneration and nurseries under village protection rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as strongly reduced, explaining that erosion from extreme rain storms is reduced by decreasing flow velocity [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__win.conditionality: The strong rating rests on thin evidence, which is why confidence is only medium. The Vietnam statement is a second-hand sentence about existing coastal forests, not planted or restored ones, gives no size or place, and its authors limit it to low and medium cyclones [ev_windbreak_protection_veettil21_1]. The India unit is a practitioner rating whose explanation describes rain-storm erosion rather than wind damage, and it covers a bundled programme, so it cannot be credited to protection alone [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. No source covers severe or extreme cyclones. Any benefit is off-site for farmers, arriving at landscape scale rather than on their plots.

forest_restoration__recurrent_cost.mechanism: Recurrent costs are annual maintenance costs per hectare entered on WOCAT sheets for regeneration, community forest and other restoration technologies in Niger, Bangladesh, India, Afghanistan, Honduras and Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_maintenance], plus a WRI table entry for eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]. A payment scheme in Costa Rica is estimated to spend between $255 and $382 per year per hectare of additional forest [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__recurrent_cost.conditionality: Values span a very wide range because the technologies and cost items differ, the WOCAT figures are compiler entries mostly converted from local currency, and the WRI figure has no price year [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]; the units from upper-middle-income countries were set aside from the class, which rests on the low- and lower-middle-income entries. The Costa Rican figure is a payment for keeping forest, expressed per hectare of forest that would not otherwise have been there, and is cited in a systematic review rather than drawn from programme accounts [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].

forest_restoration__rural_poverty.mechanism: Forest restoration reduces rural poverty mainly by creating new or additional income: forestry wages, non-timber forest products, payments for environmental services, and labour tied to restoration programmes. In Albania and Honduras, World Bank-supported participatory forest management was associated with household income rising by an estimated 30% and 62% [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3], and in Malawian co-managed forest reserves participating households had higher forestry income and owned more durable assets than non-participants [ev_household_income_kimwanga26_1, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_8]. A preprint review, not yet peer reviewed, cites economic models suggesting that the pollination benefits of forest restoration could fully outweigh its costs, especially where forest cover is already at least 10% [ev_economic_return_yang24_1].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty.conditionality: Seven sources measured a harmful economic outcome: a GEF sustainable forest management portfolio had a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69, below its cost [ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1], a Madagascar scheme was not profitable [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1], and in Malawi participants in some reserves held fewer durable assets than non-participants after rainfall shocks [ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_11, ev_farm_asset_index_kimwanga26_14]. Benefits fall unequally, with poorer and low-caste households often gaining much less from the same community forestry programmes [ev_household_income_iufro20_3], and only a minority of World Bank protected-area projects achieved their livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]. Much of the evidence is income or returns standing in for poverty, many figures are evaluation estimates or review citations without a comparison group, and the pollination result is a model cited second-hand in a preprint.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: In the high-income contexts the evidence is about payments for reforestation in north-west Costa Rica. Payments for environmental services represent 18.66% of participants' economy relative to their other income during the contract period, and the programme's overall economic impact scored 63.9%, mainly by covering a substantial part of the costs producers incur in establishing and maintaining the plantation, with family employment and legal security over the property the main perceived benefits [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: This is a small base from one survey of participants: the income share is a share of income during the contract, not a change against non-participants, and the impact score is a perception index rather than measured welfare [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3]. The plantations are commercial reforestation under contract, so the gain rests on the payments, and the benefits declined for later contract cohorts as payments were not updated while labour and transaction costs rose. The mangrove cost comparison in this row is not a household benefit and does not set the direction: mangrove restoration projects reported a median cost of US$0.1 per square metre (range 0.05–6.43) and an average replacement cost ratio of 5 (95% CI 3.1–6.9) against breakwaters giving the same wave reduction, a saving in engineering cost that accrues to society [ev_frmg_nara16_3].

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings, community and participatory forest management reach poor households mainly through forest income, wages and consumption. In a rigorous analysis of 18,000 community forests in Nepal, community forest management reduced both poverty and deforestation [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2], and a global review of community forest management records incomes increased in 68% of the 316 cases reporting on livelihoods [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1]; community forest management in Madagascar had a small but beneficial impact on household living standards, particularly for those closer to forests and with more education [ev_household_income_iufro20_2]. In a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by a mean of 26 per cent and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure near Ethiopian participatory forest management by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest while poorer households compensated for lost land access received an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. Household survey data around GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show income gains, in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically, and an Ethiopian area-closure WOCAT compiler rates farm income as improved through selling grass and wood [ev_household_income_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_robertson05_1, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: Gains are uneven and concentrate among better-off households. The community-forest review that reports income gains in 68% of cases also records 26% with no change and only 6.3% with decreases, and it pools community with household income [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1]. Near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests forest income rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; in Nepal, benefits of community forest management to poor and low caste households are often much less than those to well-off households [ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not economically profitable for lack of valid alternatives, and the Gelose transfers raised neither community incomes nor the money usable in the area [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions to household income in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor [ev_household_income_iufro20_4]. Most units are forest-governance instruments rather than restoration practices, many are secondary citations in reviews, the Albania, Honduras and Andhra Pradesh figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh increment measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group, and apart from the Nepal poverty analysis every unit measures income, consumption or returns as a proxy for poverty [ev_household_income_ieg13_4, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2].

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: Payments for environmental services raise household income on average: a meta-analysis of payment programmes in low- and middle-income countries finds a positive effect on overall household income (standardised mean difference [SMD] = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: The gain does not come from farming: the same meta-analysis finds no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11, 95% CI [−0.06, 0.29]), on income from nonagricultural sources (0.05 SMD) or on household assets (SMD = 0.04) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2]. Livelihood components of conservation projects often fail: just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]. The row rests on a single systematic review with meta-analysis and a single portfolio evaluation; income is a proxy for poverty, and both concern payment and protection programmes for existing forest rather than restoration.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings income gains come from subsidies, payments and forest products. China's Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, afforestation subsidies increased off-farm labour earnings, and the programme's benefits exceeded its costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9, ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]. Community forestry in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]; secondary forest regeneration coupled with palm-fruit harvest improved farmer income in Brazil's Atlantic forest [ev_household_income_iufro20_10]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually [ev_household_income_ieg13_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1], and WOCAT compilers in Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate long-term returns against costs as favourable [ev_economic_return_wocat_1523_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1529_2012_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4367_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: Harm and null findings sit alongside the gains. REDD+ sites in Indonesia showed potentially harmful effects on well-being, and Brazil's Reflorestar payments programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment [ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_economic_return_seixas24_1]. In Mexico the PSAH payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2]. Around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. The Chinese gains are subsidy-driven and the Wuqi figure has no counterfactual, the Colombian figure is a carbon valuation rather than cash income [ev_economic_return_wri17_3], the Amazon returns are modelled, and the payment and benefit-cost figures are cited in systematic reviews. Food-security findings now sit on the food-insecurity row, and plantation results, including Vietnam's smallholder plantations and Latin American payments for reforestation plantings, are reported in their own family rows; neither counts toward this row.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes, and the sub-practice rows agree on that direction. A UNESCO review of moist tropical forest hydrology locates the surface protection in the litter and herb layer: erosion is minimal where the soil surface is protected by a well-developed litter and herb layer, rises only slightly when the understorey is removed, and rises dramatically when the litter layer is destroyed or removed [ev_erosion_hazard_bruij90_10]. The same review states that tree planting, like soil conservation measures, may well reduce the sediment from surface erosion and shallow land slips entering the drainage system [ev_sediment_retention_bruij90_13]. In the passive regeneration evidence, an Ethiopian meta-analysis finds areas closed for grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1], the Tanzanian enclosure compiler rates surface runoff as decreased as a result of vegetation cover and downstream siltation as decreased through improved vegetation cover and controlled erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1607_2014_downstream_siltation], and the higher probability of landslides after timber removal diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. The planting evidence carries the measured magnitudes: in Pakistan a watershed restoration reduced storm runoff and sediment yields by 55 and 78% [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_1, ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1], Chir pine planting with elimination of grazing at Balakot reduced surface runoff by 57% and sediment production by 69% against adjacent grazed land [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2], tree planting on degraded Ethiopian catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2], and vegetation restoration in China could reduce soil erosion by at least 80% once cover exceeds 60% [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1]. A Slovak catchment model shows reforestation decreasing surface runoff [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1]. A meta-analysis of vegetation restoration in erosion zones finds that both forestland and grassland restoration of cropland or bare land were effective methods for controlling erosion, cutting sediment and runoff, with canopies, root systems and the organic surface layer not differing in their impact [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1, ev_runoff_reduction_yang23_2]. In Tigray, Ethiopia, upstream treatment with deep trenches, percolation pits and afforestation reduced siltation of May Demu dam by up to 60%, a figure the chapter takes from Woldearegay's earlier 2011 report, and in the Abreha Weatsbeha watershed the authors observed significant improvements in reducing soil erosion after afforestation, area closures and water-harvesting works [ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_3, ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_1]. FAO syntheses call forest restoration one of the best ways of reducing sedimentation in degraded cleared land, list reducing soil loss among the very good reasons for rehabilitating watersheds, and cite Taiwan, where a rehabilitation programme reduced reservoir sedimentation by 55 percent of the base rate [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. An FAO review of forests and landslides in Asia asserts that tree planting on susceptible slopes can reduce risk [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_1], and land abandonment with an increase in forest and grassland led to less soil erosion in one cited case [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_5]. At community-managed sites the India compiler credits trees and other vegetation with mitigating displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands and with slowing sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation], and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.conditionality: The benefit is largely off-site for farmers: much of it is reduced runoff and sediment reaching downstream land and channels rather than better soil on their own plots [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. Scale and time limit the downstream effect. The UNESCO review warns that, because of storage effects, it may take several decades for basins larger than several hundred square kilometres before stream sediment loads downstream become noticeably smaller [ev_sediment_retention_bruij90_14]. Nulls and dissent stay named. In China the soil conservation measures, including vegetation and engineering, contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction in the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area, so the vegetation share should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]; decreased Pearl River sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3]; and on the Loess Plateau an inversely decreasing trend of erosion reduction with vegetation cover was attributed to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. A Himalayan position paper judges that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_ives87_1], young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support of its older predecessors [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5], abandoned land in previously terraced landscapes can be particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4], and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The largest measured reductions are bundles: the Pakistan results combine planting with grazing control and, in the watershed study, erosion control structures, and the Taiwan programme combines reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, so none can be credited to tree cover alone [ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The Tigray results are bundles of afforestation and area closures with trenches, percolation pits and check-dams, from showcase sites, and the dam figure is an upper bound carried from an earlier report [ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_3, ev_erosion_hazard_woldearegay17_1]. The UNESCO sediment statement also offers tree planting as one option among soil conservation measures, not as a measured tree effect [ev_sediment_retention_bruij90_13]. The erosion-zone meta-analysis reports its forest-only effect sizes only in a figure, so it sets the direction but not a size [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1]. The runoff results measure a component of erosion risk rather than soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Studies of what existing forest does, including logging and harvest landslide studies, sit in the protection family row and do not count here, and plantation results are kept in their own family row, out of this roll-up.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: In high-income settings the row rests on three units, and none is a measured plot-level soil-loss study. A catchment model of Slovakia's Hornad watershed finds that reforestation results in decreasing surface runoff and flood volume, though it raises interflow, baseflow and evapotranspiration [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1]. In Taiwan, reservoir sedimentation from 1965 until 1985 was reduced by 55 percent of the base rate set from 1957 data, attributed to a rehabilitation programme [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. A US report cites the conclusion that young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support that its much larger and older predecessors did, so slope protection returns only as the forest matures [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The evidence is thin. The Hornad result is a model scenario and covers runoff, a component of erosion risk, not soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1]. The Taiwan reduction is credited to a bundled programme of reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, cited in an FAO review, so it cannot be credited to tree cover alone [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The US root-support point is cited second-hand from an earlier study, and it is about how slowly regrowth restores protection, not a measured erosion change [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5]. Missing here: a measured soil-loss or sediment comparison between restored and unrestored land in a high-income setting. The row applies only to high-income contexts and does not transfer directly to low-income settings. Plantation results are kept in their own family rows, out of forest restoration.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings, planting, area closure and regeneration reduce runoff and the soil it carries. In the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation from sheet erosion fell 55 percent and 78 percent five years after tree planting and closure of slopes to grazing [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1]; in Ethiopia, a meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and tree planting on degraded catchments reduced annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Uganda, Tanzania, Niger, Tunisia, India, Bangladesh, Tajikistan and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4372_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss]: an Ethiopian compiler reports an initial 50% reduction in soil loss after 2–3 years, the Tanzanian compiler controlled soil erosion through vegetation cover, and the Indian compiler says trees and other vegetation helped mitigate displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: An Ethiopian area-closure compiler rates downstream siltation as worse, and the Tajikistan compiler rates only a slight decrease in soil loss [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than measurements, some sheets bundle planting with structures (an Ethiopian compiler attributes reduced siltation to sediments deposited behind the bund), and the Pakistan result combines planting with grazing exclusion [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5]. The Ethiopian meta-analysis values are runoff coefficients and depths, a component of erosion risk rather than measured soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. One measured governance result is null: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1], cited in a systematic review.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: World Bank projects using participatory forest management reported reduced soil erosion among their environmental outcomes, where those outcomes were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis reports the opposite in a particular setting: particularly serious erosion in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard, or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The two sources are separated by management of the ground layer, which is a design choice: the erosion problem is tied to stripping vegetation and litter beneath plantations [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3], whereas the reduction is reported for participatory management of forests [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. For scoping, the sentence that matters is to keep understorey and litter in place; trees alone do not protect the soil. Neither side is strong: one is a portfolio evaluation narrative without magnitudes that covers only projects that monitored the outcome, with possible positive-reporting bias, and the other is a cited general statement about plantations; neither measures soil loss.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the evidence is a critical review of China's vegetation restoration programmes, which plant trees, shrubs and grass on hillslopes, a review of erosion in steep tropical terrain, and a meta-analysis of vegetation restoration in erosion zones. Restored cover protects soil once it is dense enough: once vegetation cover exceeds 60%, the restoration strategy could reduce soil erosion by at least 80%, while below that threshold the erosion-reduction benefit rises sharply with cover [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1]. In Leyte, Philippines, recovering forest on former slash-and-burn land generated the smallest share of overland flow among the land uses compared, behind fallow pasture, hedgerow systems and mulched cornfields [ev_runoff_reduction_sidle06_1], and on harvested slopes the higher probability of landslides diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. A meta-analysis of vegetation restoration in erosion zones finds that both forestland and grassland restoration of cropland or bare land were effective methods for controlling erosion, cutting sediment and runoff, with canopies, root systems and the organic surface layer not differing in their impact [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1, ev_runoff_reduction_yang23_2].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The class is capped at moderate because few of the units that point the same way say how big the effect is, and the Chinese review itself bounds the gain. In the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area, soil conservation measures including vegetation and engineering contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction, so the contribution from vegetation restoration should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]. On the Pearl River the decreased sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures over 20 years [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3], and in 12 small Loess Plateau watersheds the erosion-reduction benefit fell as cover rose, attributed to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. The benefit therefore depends on cover reaching a high threshold and on plantings maturing, and young or sparse restoration may do little. The erosion-zone meta-analysis reports its forest-only effect sizes only in a figure, so it sets the direction but not a size [ev_erosion_hazard_yang23_1]. The Philippine and landslide results are cited secondary findings, the landslide one tracking regrowth after timber harvest without separating replanting from natural regeneration [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. Benefits fall largely off-site for farmers, as less sediment downstream.

forest_restoration__water_quality_risk.mechanism: Lower sediment load is the component of water quality this row rests on. WOCAT compilers in Tanzania and India rate downstream siltation as decreased, the Tanzanian compiler as a result of improved vegetation cover and controlled erosion and the Indian compiler because the technology helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1607_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. An FAO forests-and-water synthesis calls forest restoration one of the best ways of reducing sedimentation in degraded areas of cleared land experiencing accelerated erosion [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1], and cites Taiwan, where reservoir sedimentation from 1965 until 1985 was reduced by 55 percent of the base rate, attributed to a rehabilitation programme [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. A UNESCO review of moist tropical forest hydrology states that tree planting, like soil conservation measures, may well reduce the sediment from surface erosion and shallow land slips entering the drainage system [ev_sediment_retention_bruij90_13].
forest_restoration__water_quality_risk.conditionality: Apart from the two reviews, the units are compiler ratings of siltation used as a component proxy, with no measured water-quality data such as nutrients or turbidity. The same UNESCO review warns that, because of storage effects, it may take several decades for basins larger than several hundred square kilometres before stream sediment loads downstream become noticeably smaller [ev_sediment_retention_bruij90_14]. The Taiwan reduction is a high-income case credited to a bundled programme of reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control, check dams, agroforestry and conservation farming, so it cannot be attributed to forest restoration alone [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The benefit falls off-site for farmers, on downstream water users and reservoirs.

forest_restoration__water_stress.mechanism: This row is about water on and under the restored land: soil water, groundwater and supply for the people who use them. Practitioners applying these technologies rate water quantity and availability as improved: in India the technologies improve the water holding capacity of the soil by decreasing runoff velocity and improve overall water storage [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity]; in Tanzania the compiler records a reduction in unproductive loss of both green and blue water [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity]; and in Afghanistan, through revegetation and improved land cover, water seeps into the ground, recharging the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability].
forest_restoration__water_stress.conditionality: Read this row as local supply. Measured groundwater-recharge evidence, which found recharge decreasing with forest cover expansion, sits in the catchment water yield rows; check wells and springs that depend on recharge there before assuming a gain. All of the weight is practitioner rating from technology sheets, several of which bundle several practices, rather than measured flow or soil moisture, and the Afghan compiler rates only a slight increase [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability]. What restoration does to the water leaving the catchment for downstream users is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings the positive evidence rests on infiltration and baseflow. In Ethiopia a meta-analysis found baseflow from catchments with exclosures 1.5 to 4 times greater than from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1], and a land-climate model projects a significant increase in water yield of 84.9% in the Irrawaddy basin under full reforestation [ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]. WOCAT compilers in India, Afghanistan, Tanzania, Tunisia and Niger rate water quantity, availability or harvesting as improved [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1568_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1626_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water]: the Indian compiler says the technologies improve the water holding capacity of the soil by decreasing runoff velocity and cites improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, the Afghan compiler that through revegetation water seeps into the ground, recharging the water table, and the Tanzanian compiler a reduction in unproductive loss of both green and blue water.
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: Compilers for area closure in Ethiopia and reforestation in Honduras rate water quantity unchanged, the Honduras compiler expecting effects of reforestation only in the long term [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1598_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_750_2016_water_quantity]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than flow measurements, several from sheets that bundle planting with other practices; the Ethiopian baseflow result compares exclosure catchments with cropland rather than with the degraded land before restoration [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1]; and the Irrawaddy gain is a model projection at basin scale [ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]. This scope holds no measured catchment evidence of the water-yield losses that afforestation causes elsewhere.

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: A global synthesis of paired catchments found that afforestation reduced annual runoff on average by 44% when grasslands and 31% when shrublands were afforested, with proportional reductions even larger for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site, suggesting more severe effects in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. Trees use the water: tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, which evaporates without reaching soil water reserves, and trees use much of the water that does soak in, so extensive reforestation or afforestation should not be expected to increase dry-season low flows [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: These results concern afforestation of grassland and shrubland in paired catchments, mostly in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand, rather than restoration of degraded forest land, so the size of the loss for restoring native forest on cleared land is not measured here [ev_water_yield_farley05_1]. The row rests on one global synthesis of measured catchments and one regional expert synthesis citing earlier work [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate water availability and the harvesting or collection of water as improved after afforestation in Cabo Verde and after afforestation of bare land in karst areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1523_2011_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_water_availability].
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: These are compiler ratings from two technology sheets, with no comment on how the gain arises and no measured flow, soil-moisture or groundwater data; the row applies to upper-middle-income contexts only. Water leaving the catchment for downstream users is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__waterlogging__all.mechanism: Compilers for an Ethiopian area closure and for closure with acacia reforestation in Tunisia rate excess-water drainage as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage]. A different Ethiopian area closure is rated as slightly worsening drainage [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage].
forest_restoration__waterlogging__all.conditionality: The sources do not say what separates the two sides: the worsening rating and one of the improving ratings both come from Ethiopian area closures, and none of the three ratings states a mechanism [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage]. All units are practitioner ratings, not measurements. The Uzbekistan and Uganda tree-planting sheets are plantation results, reported in their own family rows and parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots.

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.mechanism: The row rests on a WOCAT compiler rating for broadleaf plantations with assisted tree regeneration in India, which rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as strongly decreased and explains that erosion impacts from extreme rain storms are reduced by decreasing flow velocity [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.conditionality: This row is data deficient. Its evidence is a single practitioner rating, not a measurement, and the comment concerns erosion under storm rainfall rather than wind, so it says nothing about shelter from cyclone winds or surge [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. A second independent source, or a measured finding on wind or storm damage near restored forest, is needed before a class can be stated; the missing class is not evidence of no effect.

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.mechanism: Compilers for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh, a programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries in India, and community reforestation of micro-basins in Honduras rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced; the India compiler attributes this to lower flow velocity reducing erosion from extreme rain storms, and the Honduras compiler to forests reducing landslide risk [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from technology sheets, not measurements, and none describes reduced wind damage: the explained ratings work through rain-storm erosion and landslides. The Bangladesh and Honduras compilers rate only a slight reduction, the Honduras compiler expecting a greater effect in the long term [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.mechanism: Mangrove planting in northern Viet Nam is credited with protecting a sea dyke that a comparable typhoon had damaged before planting, and with cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent; planted mangroves in Hainan, China reduced mean wind speed behind the stand during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. Compilers rate mangrove buffers in the Philippines as reducing cyclone impacts and afforestation in Cabo Verde and saxaul dune belts in Turkmenistan as lowering wind speed, by 20-25% in the saxaul belts [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_578_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1529_2012_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.conditionality: The Viet Nam figures are uncontrolled before-and-after comparisons attributed to mangroves by the implementing Red Cross programme's evaluators. The Cabo Verde and Turkmenistan ratings concern everyday wind, not cyclones, and all WOCAT units are practitioner ratings.
